  - region "Simple English explanation of Parameter Explorer":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Parameter Explorer" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A parameter controls a family of graphs. In y=ax+b, a is slope and b is the vertical shift, while x is the input along one graph. Changing a tilts every line; changing x only moves the point. A useful rule is Parameter model: y=a x+b. You can learn Parameter Explorer by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Change one parameter at a time, keep x as the axis variable, and watch which feature moves. Example: In y=ax+b, which parameter shifts the line vertically? b is added to every y. b. So the answer is b."
    - paragraph: "In real life, simulations: A slider changes model assumptions. Watch out: Treating a like the input x. A parameter controls the rule; x is the input."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: In y=ax+b, which parameter shifts the line vertically?
      - generic "Compare your answer"
